text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Transport minister Tuula Linnainmaa says Finland would levy tolls on Russian cargo trucks in retaliation if Russian duma sets proposed border fees for Finnish trucks.
- Air UK abandons plans to become first ever foreign airline to fly domestic routes in Finland due to aircraft shortage.
- Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen visiting Latvia strongly criticised those urging Baltic states to join Nato.
- EU commissioned research finds no health risks in using digital mobile phones but final conclusions cannot yet be drawn, experts say.
- Travel sales increased in Finland last year but travel agencies' earnings did not rise.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Foreign-owned Finnish firms have been more profitable than others, study shows.
- JP Morgan finds post and telephone operator PT Finland interesting to investors, should the government decide to float part of it.
- Competition between electricity utilities paves ways for small- and medium-sized companies to choose supplier but the process is slowed by expensive measuring equipment.
- Mutual insurer Tapiola tightens grip of its clients by offering discounts at the turn of the year.
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto sees no external risk that Finland would be excluded from the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
- Meeting-mania spreads among Finnish companies -- often a sign of managers avoiding responsibility, auditor says.
- Former Suunto owners, the Niemisto family, on Monday bought large amounts of shares in retail and department store group Stockmann.
- Banking sector cross-border mergers in Europe will continue and traditional banks and insurance companies will disappear, predicts BZW chairman Peter Middleton.
- Bank of Finland official says revision of pension funds' investment system insufficient, unclear and lacking transparency. Calls for venture capital investments from pension funds.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET

- Aktia Bank replaces head of treasury Peter Storsjo with Mikael Ingberg who will leave Pellervo Institute of Economic Research. Ingberg to take charge of funds, brokerage and private banking while CEO Johan Horelli says will lead rest of treasury.
- Poet Solveig von Schoultz died on Tuesday at age 89, just a couple of months after publishing her last collection.

- Leasing temporary clerical personnel increasingly common and the business is expected to continue to grow in the next few years. Nowegian-American group Olsten Corporation enters the Finnish market.

- Nokia has become one of the best-known brands in Israel as mobile phone penetration there nears Finland's world-leading level. Nokia has sold almost a third or 300,000 mobile phones in the country since entering the market in 1994.
TURUN SANOMAT
- The EU's food aid to Finland's poor will be reduced to a third or 12 million markka next year.
-- Roland Moller, Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 242
